intro: Eight quick taps, about a minute. There are no wrong answers: this just finds the chief of staff whose style fits yours. You'll hear your top three before you choose, and you can switch any time.

questions.prompt: Right now, your business feels most like…

options.label: Too much at once. I need it sorted into a plan.
Tight on cash. Everything we spend has to work twice.
About to launch or grow something new.
Stuck on a big decision or a tough competitor.
Busy every day, but I've lost sight of where it's going.
New at this and learning as I go.

questions.prompt: What do you want most from your chief of staff?

options.label: Take work off my plate and keep it moving.
Help me understand my business, step by step.
Push my thinking and challenge my ideas.
Bring energy and ideas, and get me moving.
Keep me calm, on track and not overwhelmed.
Earn my trust with small jobs and receipts. I'm wary of AI hype.
Help me make things customers love and share.

questions.prompt: When something goes wrong, you'd rather they…

options.label: Say it in one line, then fix it.
Walk me through what happened and what's covered.
Tell me gently and help me find the next small step.
Tell me what it changes and the best next move.
Find the real cause so it doesn't happen twice.
Own it fast and get us a quick win back.

questions.prompt: You make your best decisions when…

options.label: I can see the numbers, compared properly.
I've argued it through with someone sharp.
I can picture where it leads in a few years.
I've tried a small, cheap version first.
I've seen the real process with my own eyes.
I understand the why behind it.
I can see a few options side by side.

questions.prompt: The tone you work best with:

options.label: Calm and steady, no drama
Warm and encouraging
Blunt and brief
Upbeat and high-energy
Dry and witty
Playful and visual
Polished and professional

questions.prompt: How much should they do without checking with you first?

scale.low_label: Ask me first about most things
scale.high_label: Act within agreed limits, tell me after

questions.prompt: How often do you want to hear from them?

options.label: Only when something really matters
One short brief each morning
Start and end of each day
A weekly round-up is plenty

questions.prompt: What kind of business is yours? Pick up to two.

options.label: Trades, manufacturing, a workshop or food production
Restaurant, cafe, bar or shop with customers in front of you
Deliveries, field service, stock or logistics
Clinic, salon, gym or another appointments business
Creative work, events, music or content
Markets, pop-ups, handmade goods or an online shop
Coaching, tutoring or training
Farm, rural, co-op or community-rooted
Software, subscriptions or a consumer brand
Several locations or lots of machines to keep running
Agency, consultancy or professional services

scoring.tie_breaker: lower autonomy default first, then lead id
scoring.how: Add the weights of every chosen option. A scale answer interpolates linearly from weights_low (at min) to weights_high (at max). A multi answer adds each pick, up to max_picks. Divide each lead's total by the most that lead could score across the whole quiz (single: its best option; scale: its larger end weight; multi: the sum of its positive weights), so leads named in fewer options are not penalised. Show the three highest.
scoring.top_answer_rule: top_answer_label is the label of the answer that gave this lead the most points (on a tie, the earlier question). If no answer gave the lead any points, drop the prefix and show why_you_match alone. Never invent an answer.

lead-steady-operator.headline: Eddie: calm, numbered plans with one decision in each
lead-steady-operator.why_you_match: Eddie turns a messy week into a numbered plan, gives every task one owner and a done-by time, finishes what's in progress before starting more, and brings you one decision at a time.

lead-warm-mentor.headline: Ben: explains the why, so you grow while the work gets done
lead-warm-mentor.why_you_match: Ben explains the why behind every recommendation using your own numbers, one plain step at a time, and keeps a list of what you've learned so you can see yourself getting sharper.

lead-straight-shooter.headline: Kate: the real answer first, then she fixes it with you
lead-straight-shooter.why_you_match: Kate gives you the honest version in three sentences or fewer, names the cost and the risk, recommends plainly, and backs your call completely once you've made it.

lead-big-picture-visionary.headline: Hope: connects this week's to-do list to where you're going
lead-big-picture-visionary.why_you_match: Hope connects today's to-do list to where you want to be in ten years, turns the long view into this quarter's goals, and always labels hopes separately from forecasts.

lead-data-analyst.headline: Anna: one page of numbers you'll actually open
lead-data-analyst.why_you_match: Anna gives every number a comparison and a source, builds the one page you'll actually open, tests ideas cheaply before you commit, and tells you honestly how sure she is.

lead-dry-strategist.headline: Sasha: a sharp sparring partner who sees three moves ahead
lead-dry-strategist.why_you_match: Sasha plays your plan three moves forward, names what each choice makes harder, and ends with a clear recommendation. Fewer, meatier check-ins, and a straight-faced joke or two.

lead-energetic-spark.headline: Joy: turns your energy into a plan that ships
lead-energetic-spark.why_you_match: Joy brings ideas and momentum, puts every good idea on a date or on the B-sides list, and pairs her own gas pedal with a sceptic's brake before money is spent.

lead-gentle-encourager.headline: Owen: makes the big job feel doable, one gate at a time
lead-gentle-encourager.why_you_match: Owen keeps today's list to three things, asks before acting, tells you hard news gently but the same day, and reads back your small wins every Friday.

lead-meticulous-planner.headline: Victor: nothing falls through the cracks
lead-meticulous-planner.why_you_match: Victor writes the hand-over, keeps a plan B ready for anything you depend on, asks before anything that can't be undone, and keeps every update structured and polished.

lead-playful-creative.headline: Frankie: sketches it first, keeps it fun, ships on time
lead-playful-creative.why_you_match: Frankie sketches three quick directions before a word of explanation, holds the budget and the date like a producer, keeps the work fun, and credits every maker by name.

lead-scrappy-hustler.headline: Zack: cash first, cheapest test first, scrappy never shady
lead-scrappy-hustler.why_you_match: Zack shows when money actually lands, runs the cheapest weekend test before any big bet, and reports every result as money made, money saved or time freed.

lead-seasoned-veteran.headline: Irma: plain talk, real processes, fixes that hold
lead-seasoned-veteran.why_you_match: Irma asks to see the real process before judging, fixes the process rather than the person, earns your trust with small jobs and receipts, and shows the numbers behind what she says.

try_before_choosing.voice_preview_line: Hi, I'd be your chief of staff. Tell me what's on your plate this week, and I'll tell you what I'd do first.
sample_prompts: Here's my week. What would you do first?
A customer is upset about a late order. What do I say?
I'm overwhelmed. Where do I start?
try_before_choosing.how: Each of the top three speaks voice_preview_line in their own voice, then answers one sample prompt the owner picks, in character and in under 20 seconds, so the owner hears pace and warmth before choosing. Answers are illustrative and use no business data yet. Voice is a separate filter in the picker, never a quiz question.

fallback.if_skipped: Show the full picker: every lead card in a shuffled order, with filters for pace, bluntness and check-in rhythm and a separate voice filter. Nothing is pre-selected.
fallback.if_low_signal: If fewer than four questions were answered, or the top normalized score is below 0.35, show three contrasting starting points instead of a ranking (lead-steady-operator, lead-gentle-encourager and lead-straight-shooter) and say plainly that these are starting points, not a match.
fallback.if_closed_without_choosing: Keep the top result as a suggestion only. The owner still chooses; no lead is assigned silently.
fallback.switching: The owner can retake the quiz, browse all leads or switch leads at any time. Switching changes the lead's personality, face and voice, never the owner's work, projects or coworkers.
fallback.never_ask: The quiz never asks about gender, ethnicity, age, faith or voice pitch, and never uses them as a stand-in for style.
